name: EXL2 (GPTQ with mixed per-tensor bitrate)
bits: 2-8 adjustable (target average bits-per-weight, e.g. 2.5 / 3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0 bpw builds)
notes:
GROUP SIZE LEFT NULL 2026-10-04 and this is a CATEGORY point, not a gap. LEFT NULL 2026-10-04 and this is a CATEGORY point, not a gap. EXL2 mixes quantization levels within a model AND can apply multiple levels to each individual linear layer to hit a target average bitrate, so there is no single group size to record. The upstream benchmark table makes this explicit by printing grpsz 128 for the GPTQ rows and '-' (not applicable) for every EXL2 row. A number here would be actively misleading. EXL2 uses the same optimization method as GPTQ and supports 2,3,4,5,6,8-bit, but mixes quantization levels within a model - and, per the upstream README, can apply multiple quantization levels to each individual linear layer - to hit any target average bitrate between 2 and 8 bpw (quant-exl2-readme). That mixed-precision layout is why it needs its own kernels and cannot be served by the Marlin/AWQ path. Weight-only: activations are 16-bit. The upstream repo is now archived with development moved to ExLlamaV3, so this record describes a format that is in maintenance, not in active development. No quality delta recorded: the README publishes throughput (Llama2-7B EXL2 4.0 bpw at 185 tok/s on a 3090 Ti, 211 on a 4090) but no perplexity or benchmark deltas vs fp16, and none was found elsewhere.
NATIVE_SUPPORT CLASSIFIED 2026-10-04: this field is still [] and that is CORRECT, but the empty list used to be ambiguous between three different states and now is not. Reason class on this record: WEIGHT-ONLY, SO STRUCTURALLY ABSENT. The bits field keeps activations in FP16, so execution is dequantize-to-FP16 then an FP16 tensor-core GEMM; there is no INT4-x-INT4 (or sub-8-bit x sub-8-bit) silicon instruction for it to target. This is a statement about the arithmetic, not an absence of investigation. Consequence for a reader: nothing further to verify - no silicon path is possible for this format as defined. The full statement of the three-way distinction, and the worked list of all 72 empty records by class, is in gotcha quant-native-support-empty-means-three-different-things. Rule of thumb for this field everywhere in the repo: if the bits field carries an 'a16', or the scheme is KV-cache-only or a llama.cpp integer storage type, an empty native_support is a DEFINITION and needs no verification; only a W4A4/W8A8/sub-8-bit format with research kernels can have an empty list that is a real finding.
